name: Burning Witch
label: Southern Lord
lede: Two EPs, a handful of near-empty rooms and Steve Albini at the board: the slowest band in Seattle left a short, crushing trail that runs straight into Sunn O))), Goatsnake and Khanate.

eras.title: Out of the Thorr's Hammer wreckage
eras.text: Thorr's Hammer lasted about six weeks. Its guitarists kept the idea of music slower and lower than anything in Seattle's grunge afterglow and found a singer who could scream over it.

years.src: Wikipedia: Thorr's Hammer · Southern Lord · The Sleeping Shaman
years.h: [[Thorr's Hammer|31c2d9e6-5f45-4b4e-9af1-aa46bbe3d4f9]] ends; Burning Witch grows out of it
years.p: Stephen O'Malley, Greg Anderson and Jamie Sykes carry on after the Norwegian vocalist Runhild Gammelsæter returns to Oslo. Wikipedia calls Burning Witch an offshoot of Thorr's Hammer.
years.xp:
Thorr's Hammer formed in Seattle's Ballard neighborhood in winter 1994–95, played two shows and recorded a demo and the Dommedagsnatt EP. Burning Witch began on Capitol Hill with the same core.

Sources differ on who played what: Wikipedia lists Sykes on bass at first, while Edgy 59 remembers him on drums.

years.h: Stuart Dahlquist and Edgy 59 complete the line-up
years.p: Bassist G. Stuart Dahlquist and vocalist Edgy 59 (Edgar Livengood) join, and the band finds its voice: a singer swinging between nasal melody and tortured screams. Edgy 59 says he met Dahlquist through a mutual friend.

years.h: Greg Anderson leaves for Los Angeles to start Goatsnake
years.p: Southern Lord says Anderson soon departed for LA to launch [[Goatsnake|ae720a02-629e-4e9b-98e7-d1f637bd5a49]], leaving [[Stephen O'Malley|d2db31eb-4469-4e8d-8ed2-b3c1bfff0c17]] to lead the band.
years.xp: Anderson later founded the Southern Lord label, which would release the band's compilation. He and O'Malley kept working together, most visibly in [[Sunn O)))|1d3da898-4fb4-4445-b704-cd7315e01789]].

eras.title: Albini and the empty rooms
eras.text: The band cut its first EP with a famous engineer, changed drummers, and played to crowds that thinned out by the second song.

years.h: Recording with [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] at Robert Lang Studios
years.p: The band tracks the songs that become the Towers... EP in Shoreline, Washington, with Albini producing.
years.xp:
Edgy 59 says Albini was connected to Dahlquist through an earlier friendship. He also says Albini didn't promote them in his magazine Descent.

The songs sat unreleased for two years.

years.p: After the Albini sessions Sykes leaves and B.R.A.D. takes over drums, the line-up on Rift.Canyon.Dreams.

q: By the second song there were 10 people left.
years.h: Ten people left by the second song
years.p: Edgy 59 recalls shows where the room was a quarter full halfway through the opener and down to about 10 people by the second song.
years.xp: He says the band shared bills with Napalm Death, At the Gates and Boris, and that he stayed focused on his own performance rather than the crowd.

years.h: Rift.Canyon.Dreams is recorded at Robert Lang Studios
years.p: O'Malley, Dahlquist, B.R.A.D. and Edgy 59 cut four songs, including "Warning Signs" and "Communion".
years.xp: Wikipedia says the EP came out on Merciless Records in an initial run of 500 copies.

eras.title: The doom lands
eras.text: Two EPs finally reach vinyl and disc just as the band ends. Sources disagree on exactly when.

years.p: The 1996 Albini session comes out as a 12-inch, about 37 minutes long.

years.h: Crippled Lucifer collects both EPs on Southern Lord
years.p: Seven tracks, 63 minutes, released on [[Greg Anderson|a8da7651-6d6f-4021-98a6-d68b35b1e4f8]]'s label. Wikipedia says printing errors on the first cover meant multiple pressings.
play: Crippled Lucifer (Seven Psalms for Our Lord of Light)

years.src: Southern Lord · Wikipedia · The Sleeping Shaman
years.p: Southern Lord says the band reunited briefly for autumn 1998 performances. Wikipedia says it disbanded that fall, after the final shows.
years.xp: Edgy 59 gives a different account: the band ended in 1997 after O'Malley moved to Europe and Sykes had moved to England.

eras.title: Everybody goes somewhere louder
eras.text: The members scatter into bands that grow much bigger than Burning Witch ever was, and the old recordings keep circulating on splits and a deluxe reissue.

years.h: Split CD with [[Goatsnake|ae720a02-629e-4e9b-98e7-d1f637bd5a49]] on Hydra Head
years.p: Burning Witch contributes "Communion" and "The Bleeder" to a split with Anderson's band.
The Dos Fatales release includes a Burning Witch version of "Rift Canyon Dreams" remixed by Randall Dunn.
years.xp: Dahlquist and B.R.A.D. both later played in Asva.

years.h: Crippled Lucifer returns as a double CD
years.p: Southern Lord's reissue restores a missing track and adds the split songs; a Daymare edition included live material. It was delayed from January 25.
O'Malley and Anderson formed Sunn O))), with Dahlquist on its first two albums. O'Malley also played in Khanate; Edgy 59 went to Sinisstar.
